public_rationale: Anthropic's October 26, 2026 filing leaves the aggregate commitment amount and amounts due in specified periods blank [e1]. Reuters reported on October 19 that OpenAI planned a 2027 listing and Anthropic was expected to debut in mid-November [e2]. These records do not establish a reconciled combined obligations total above $1.3 trillion, payment commencement after the IPOs for most committed dollars, or a specific material misleading disclosure [e1, e2].
limitations: The combined total lacks a consistent accounting basis and a non-overlapping contractual schedule.
The evidence does not establish the extent of non-cancellability or a complete payment-commencement schedule.
Blank disclosure fields do not establish either a lower obligations total or that investors were materially misled.

statement.excerpt: The two biggest companies — OpenAI and Anthropic — have over $1.3 trillion in obligations, many of them non-cancellable, and are looking to take their companies public before most of them kick in, tricking retail investors into believing they’re in a much better place just before the anvil drops on their head.

from_speaker: looking to take their companies public
before most of them kick in
our_interpretation: Assess the outstanding commitments and IPO plans described as current during October 2026 through the post date, including contractual updates disclosed after quarter-end.
Obligations means outstanding contractual payment commitments. Financing raised, supplier investment plans, and aspirational spending targets do not automatically qualify.
Avoid counting the same obligation twice through both a supplier arrangement and an aggregate commitments total.
Read most by committed dollars, because the statement emphasizes financial burden; the speaker does not specify this denominator.
Read kick in as commencement of contractual payments, not the date the agreement was signed or the date its expense appears in earnings.

The post identifies company disclosures for some Anthropic amounts but does not establish a consistent source or accounting basis for the combined $1.3 trillion figure. Its aggregate basis is therefore unknown.
Non-cancellability and IPO timing are asserted components of an observation, not antecedents of a conditional forecast.
Tricking investors requires a specific material misrepresentation or omission; large disclosed obligations alone do not establish it.
criteria.support_condition: A reconciled, non-overlapping schedule establishes more than $1.3 trillion of combined outstanding obligations, substantial non-cancellable commitments, IPO plans preceding payment commencement for most of the committed dollars, and material misleading offering disclosures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comprehensive comparable schedule places the combined amount at or below $1.3 trillion, or authoritative cancellation, payment, IPO, or disclosure records refute a specified material component. Incomplete disclosures alone cannot establish a lower total.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable outstanding-obligation schedules for both companies through October 28, 2026, reconciled to binding contracts, cancellation provisions and payment-start dates; IPO timing records; and offering disclosures sufficient to identify or refute a specific material misstatement or omission.
